data.translation: Darauf holt man die gepflückten Trauben und taucht siehinein. Man geht und breitet sie hin und macht so eine trockne Lage daraus.

data.turoyo: Annaqqa budewo u qṭofo daž žabaš, bəṯər qəṭfiwo ak karme maʕ ʕənwe saymiwo dibəs w saymiwo ḥarire w saymiwo ʕqude w saymiwo pastiq...
data.translation: Then the picking of the watermelons would begin; afterwards they would harvest the vineyards, and from the grapes they would make syrup, make flour-thickened grape must, make walnut sweets, and make fruit leather...

rationale: Third Infinitiv I.1 after round 1; harvest event as onset subject, with explicit watermelon patient. Jan translation is machine-generated.

data.translation: Ich ging wieder hin, aß in dem Garten Äpfel, aß Apfelsirren und Bananen, pflückte Trauben und aß sie.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (63/115)

data.turoyo: Bu sabab d i naqqa ḥreto d rawəxwo aʕle, fəšwole taqrib d ʕəsri yawme ʕal ḥaṣe, hama xayifo rahəṭ w azzeyo l bayn u bəstono, qṭəflele ʕənwe w disa ḥṣirile bi maḥsarto w fayəš məqdar d ḥamšaḥṣar yawme ḥrene bu ʕaḏabano.
data.translation: Weil nun das vorige Mal der Kerl, der auf mir ritt, fast zwanzig Tage auf meinem Rücken geblieben war, lief ich diesmal gleich in den Garten, pflückte mir Trauben und presste sie in der Kelter; und so blieb ich nur fünfzehn Tage in dieser Qual.

rationale: Preterit thin cell; third-person beneficiary counterpart qṭəflele, preserving narrative perspective.

data.turoyo: Aʕ+ʕənwaṯṯe, dəmmina, meqəm quṭfíwanne mas+sate, mak+karme. Ġayṭíwanne bam+maye, šəkəl dmaye, saymiwa šəkəl dmaye. Maye du+zeyoto kummínanne.

data.translation: Wenn man nun die Buttermilch erhitzt, steigt das Wasser nach oben, das man abschöpfte. (Den Bodensatz) pflegten sie in einen Stoffbeutel zu schütten und machten daraus den ǧaǧiq, wie sie ihn nannten.

data.translation: Den Ayran schlürft man so mit Brot. Manche Leute "wärmen ihn auch an und tun ihn in ein Kochgeschirr; dann steigt das Wasser davon in die Höhe. Dann schöpft man das gelbliche Wasser davon ab.

rationale: Independent second text supports technical sense2; explicit liquid and source me aʕlayye.

summary: Harvesting is transitive with unmarked picked product or object suffix; qṭəflili/qṭəflele add a beneficiary. Source phrases include m- and ʕal.

The dairy sense is not inferred from translation alone: rising maye is explicitly resumed by plural -nne and removed me aʕlayye in another text. Do not identify the subsequent singular bagged residue with that water without checking.
The inherited Detransitive is a complexion state/change rather than literal picking; Part. Pass. qṭife newly supplies the literal result. Its sense numbering is explicitly separated.
Reader reports of two Preterit examples overcount a Russian note. The actual supplied parsed entry has one Preterit example with that note attached; no erroneous extra example exists to delete.
No new idiomatic phrase is established. The new dairy meaning is a lexical technical verb sense, not a light-verb collocation.

Round 2 only. Jan English is project machine translation, retained verbatim in selected excerpts; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are retained as the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.

Round 1 already introduced Infinitiv, literal Detransitive Part. Pass. and dairy skimming I.2. Reader statements that Infinitiv is absent are stale. Jan strengthens the existing Infinitiv cell rather than proposing it again.

After round 1, Preterit I.1 has five examples and Infectum/Infectum-wa have four each. Routine harvesting predicates do not justify further additions to those populated cells. The repeated qṭofo and qəṭfiwo tokens receive separate decisions but one context is not repeatedly quoted.
The seasonal ordering of vegetable plots, vineyards and subsequent livestock slaughter supplies agricultural discourse evidence. No new sense or idiom is established.
Confirm in JTM2.5/7 that plural quṭfiwunne refers to rising water, with following singular -le referring to residue;94/197 independently confirms water skimming.
Confirm whether qṭofo/qṭofayḏe are productive Infinitiv. They denote the active picking process and lack Detransitive morphology; no Detransitive Infinitiv is proposed.
Check whether pallor qṭəfina is felt as figurative use of picking or a separate homonym; retained in the inherited root with its own Detransitive sense.
